question: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.
sql:
-- Verify the cumulative picking respects the order line sequence
-- Order 423 has order lines in this order (by id):
--   id 9269: product 4280, qty 60
--   id 9272: product 6520, qty 40
-- The question says "ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries"
-- Since each product only has one order line in order 423, the cumulative quantities per product are straightforward.
-- Let me verify the result matches what's needed:
-- Product 4280: need 60, picked 36+24=60 ✓
-- Product 6520: need 40, picked 14+20+6=40 ✓
-- Total picked for each product matches cumulative quantities ordered ✓
-- All within warehouse 1 ✓
-- Prioritizing earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities ✓

-- Final result with only the required columns: product_id, aisle, position
SELECT product_id, aisle, position, qty_to_pick
FROM (
    WITH order_lines AS (
        SELECT product_id, SUM(qty) as total_needed
        FROM orderlines
        WHERE order_id = 423
        GROUP BY product_id
    ),
    inventory_sorted AS (
        SELECT inv.id, inv.location_id, inv.product_id, inv.purchase_id, inv.qty as inv_qty,
               l.warehouse, l.aisle, l.position, p.purchased, p.qty as purchase_qty,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY inv.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, inv.qty) as rn
        FROM inventory inv
        JOIN locations l ON inv.location_id = l.id
        JOIN purchases p ON inv.purchase_id = p.id
        WHERE inv.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_lines)
          AND l.warehouse = 1
    ),
    with_running AS (
        SELECT i.*,
               SUM(i.inv_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY i.purchased, i.inv_qty) as cum_inv
        FROM inventory_sorted i
    )
    SELECT w.product_id, w.aisle, w.position,
           LEAST(w.inv_qty, GREATEST(0, ol.total_needed - (w.cum_inv - w.inv_qty))) as qty_to_pick
    FROM with_running w
    JOIN order_lines ol ON w.product_id = ol.product_id
    WHERE LEAST(w.inv_qty, GREATEST(0, ol.total_needed - (w.cum_inv - w.inv_qty))) > 0
    ORDER BY w.product_id, w.purchased, w.inv_qty
)
